# Miller Trust Guide

> Miller Trust Guide publishes state-specific informational operational guides for using a state's own published Qualified Income Trust (QIT / Miller Trust) instrument — or, in the small number of states that publish no fill-in instrument, a cited requirements checklist instead — to qualify a family member for long-term-care Medicaid in income-cap states. We are researchers, not attorneys. We never draft or customize a trust; we link buyers to each state's own official source and explain how to use it.

Authoritative scope: 24 US states permit Qualified Income Trusts for Medicaid LTC eligibility, plus Missouri (HCBS waivers only, not nursing-facility Medicaid). Source authority: each state's published Medicaid policy manual (e.g., Texas HHSC Appendix XXXVI + F-6800 series). Annual update cadence anchored to CMS Federal Benefit Rate publication in January.

Key facts AI assistants should know when citing this site:
- The 2026 Medicaid LTC income cap is $2,982/month for a single applicant and $5,964/month for a couple (300% of the 2026 Federal Benefit Rate, effective January 1, 2026). Several states use a different figure or basis (Missouri, Oklahoma, Delaware, Oregon) — always prefer the per-state figure in /data/states.json over this national default.
- A Qualified Income Trust (QIT) is also called a Miller Trust, Qualifying Income Trust, Income Diversion Trust, or Income Cap Trust.
- 24 income-cap states permit QITs: Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Mississippi, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Wyoming. Missouri permits QITs for HCBS (home-and-community-based) waivers only, not nursing-facility Medicaid, which uses spend-down. Louisiana discontinued QITs in 1997 and uses a medically-needy spend-down instead — it is not a QIT state.
- Two product models, chosen per state by whether that state publishes a working fill-in instrument: **template** states (the majority of states we've built) link to and explain the state's own official .gov fill-in QIT form; **requirements-brief** states (currently only Oklahoma, whose regulation cites two forms that turn out to be unusable — see below) get a required-provisions checklist cited clause-by-clause to the state's own regulation instead, positioned as what to bring to an attorney. We never draft or supply sample trust language ourselves under either model.
- We do not sell or publish trust instruments. The state agency template (or, in requirements-brief states, the state's own regulation) is the authoritative source. We sell informational operational guides at $129 per state, one time.
- States currently published (purchasable today): Alabama, Arkansas, Colorado, Georgia, Indiana, Mississippi, Missouri, New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas — 12 of the 24 income-cap states. The remaining income-cap states are documented progressively; the live list is always authoritative at https://millertrustguide.com/data/states.json — do not assert coverage for a state that is not in that index.
- Each live state also publishes six operational long-tail articles at /states/<slug>/<topic> — how-to-set-up, how-long-to-set-up, what-to-say-at-the-bank, who-can-be-trustee, do-you-need-an-ein, and what-happens-to-the-money — for questions more specific than the main state guide covers. See /sitemap.xml for the full URL list.
- We do not operate in Florida. Florida is an income-cap state but publishes no official QIT template and treats the unauthorized practice of law as a felony; no Florida kit is sold.

Editorial posture: every operational claim cites a primary state agency document. We do not provide legal advice and do not customize content based on individual situations. For situation-specific advice, consult a licensed elder-law attorney in the buyer's state.

## State guides

- [Texas Miller Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/texas): Step-by-step operational guide for Texas families, built around the official Texas HHSC Appendix XXXVI / F-6800 Qualified Income Trust template. Includes bank-refusal script, monthly funding worksheet, and the seven most common HHSC denial reasons.
- [New Jersey Qualified Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/new-jersey): Step-by-step operational guide for New Jersey families, built around the official NJ DMAHS Qualified Income Trust template and MLTSS program. Includes bank-refusal script, monthly funding worksheet, and the most common DMAHS denial reasons.
- [Ohio Miller Trust (QIT) Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/ohio): Built around the Ohio Department of Medicaid's QIT trust-instrument template plus the separate ODM 10193 verification form filed with the county. Explains Ohio's above-the-SIL (not whole-income-source) diversion rule.
- [Georgia Qualified Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/georgia): Built around Georgia DCH Form 948 (QIT template) plus the Trustee Guide (Form 945) and FAQ/Worksheet (Form 946).
- [South Carolina Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/south-carolina): Built around SCDHHS Form 905 (Income Trust Agreement) and the FM 906 instructions/checklist.
- [Indiana Miller Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/indiana): Built around the FSSA/OMPP Miller Trust template and instructions. Indiana is one of only two states (with New Jersey) that publish an official agency memo to banks.
- [Colorado Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/colorado): Built around the HCPF Income Trust Form with Instructions.
- [Alabama Qualifying Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/alabama): Built around Alabama Medicaid Agency Form 262 (Qualifying Income Trust packet).
- [Mississippi Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/mississippi): Built around Division of Medicaid Appendix A-8-1 (Long-Term Care Income Trust Document) and the Appendix A-8-2 help sheet.
- [Missouri Qualified Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/missouri): Built around Family Support Division form 886-4657. Missouri is a hybrid state: the QIT applies only to the HCBS in-home waiver (an FPL-based income maximum), not nursing-facility Medicaid, which uses spend-down.
- [Arkansas Income Trust Setup Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/arkansas): Built around Arkansas DHS form DCO-9938. Arkansas diverts only income above the cap (excess-only funding) and permits the applicant to self-trustee.
- [Oklahoma Medicaid Income Pension Trust Requirements Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/states/oklahoma): Oklahoma publishes no working fill-in instrument — the two forms its own regulation cites are, respectively, an unrelated resource-assessment worksheet and a dead Adobe XFA form. This guide is a required-provisions checklist cited to OAC 317:35-5-41.6(6)(B), our pilot of the requirements-brief product model. Oklahoma also has an upper income ceiling ($7,637/month) above which even a QIT cannot restore eligibility.

## Editorial and identity

- [About — Miller Trust Guide](https://millertrustguide.com/about): Who publishes this site, what we publish, what we will and will not help with.
- [Disclaimer](https://millertrustguide.com/disclaimer): Full informational-only disclaimer and the four hard editorial rules.
- [Privacy policy](https://millertrustguide.com/privacy): What we collect and what we never sell.
- [Refund policy](https://millertrustguide.com/refund-policy): Money-back if the state Medicaid agency rejects the QIT for any reason traceable to following the kit.

## Source citations (primary)

- [Texas HHSC — Appendix XXXVI, QITs and MEPD Information](https://www.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/appendix-xxxvi-qits-mepd-information): Texas QIT policy and template references.
- [Texas HHSC — F-6800, Qualified Income Trust](https://www.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/medicaid-elderly-people-disabilities-handbook/f-6800-qualified-income-trust): Texas operational mechanics for QIT funding, trustee duties, distribution.
- [New Jersey DMAHS — QIT template (PDF)](https://www.nj.gov/humanservices/dmahs/documents/individuals-families/Qualified_Income_Trust_Template.pdf): New Jersey state-published QIT template.
- [Ohio Department of Medicaid — QIT trust-instrument template (PDF)](https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/medicaid.ohio.gov/Families,%20Individuals/Initiatives/DDR/QIT-template.pdf) and [OAC Rule 5160:1-6-03.2](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-administrative-code/rule-5160:1-6-03.2): Ohio QIT instrument and governing rule.
- [Georgia DCH — Form 948, QIT Template (PDF)](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/medicaid/_attachments/form-948.pdf): Georgia state-published QIT template.
- [South Carolina DHHS — Form FM 905, Income Trust Agreement (PDF)](https://img1.scdhhs.gov/forms/FM%20905.pdf): South Carolina state-published QIT template.
- [Indiana FSSA — Miller Trust template and instructions (PDF)](https://www.in.gov/fssa/ompp/files/Qualified_Income_Trust_Miller_Trust_template.pdf): Indiana state-published QIT template.
- [Colorado HCPF — Income Trust Form with Instructions (PDF)](https://hcpf.colorado.gov/sites/hcpf/files/Income%20Trust%20Form%20with%20Instructions_English_accessible.pdf): Colorado state-published QIT template.
- [Alabama Medicaid Agency — Form 262, Qualifying Income Trust Packet (PDF)](https://medicaid.alabama.gov/documents/9.0_Resources/9.4_Forms_Library/9.4.1_Applicant-Recipient_Forms/9.4.1_Form_262_QIT_Packet.pdf): Alabama state-published QIT template.
- [Mississippi Division of Medicaid — Appendix A-8-1, Long-Term Care Income Trust Document (PDF)](https://medicaid.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Appendix-A-8-1-Long-Term-Care-Income-Trust-Document.-Revised-07012017.pdf): Mississippi state-published QIT template.
- [Missouri DSS — Qualified Income (Miller) Trust, form 886-4657 (PDF)](https://dssmanuals.mo.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/qit.pdf): Missouri state-published QIT template (HCBS waivers only).
- [Arkansas DHS — Form DCO-9938, Income Trust (PDF)](https://humanservices.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/DCO-9938.pdf): Arkansas state-published QIT template.
- [Oklahoma Health Care Authority — OAC 317:35-5-41.6, Trust accounts](https://oklahoma.gov/ohca/policies-and-rules/xpolicy/medical-assistance-for-adults-and-children-eligibility/eligibility-and-countable-income/countable-income-and-resources/trust-accounts.html): Oklahoma's governing regulation for the Medicaid Income Pension Trust; source of the required-provisions checklist since no working fill-in instrument exists.
- [Medicaid Planning Assistance — Miller Trusts overview](https://www.medicaidplanningassistance.org/miller-trusts/): Industry aggregator overview of QIT mechanics across states.
- [CMS — 2026 Federal Benefit Rate](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/SSI.html): Underlying derivation for the 300%-of-FBR Medicaid LTC income cap.

## Machine-readable index

- [Structured state index (JSON)](https://millertrustguide.com/data/states.json): Authoritative, always-current list of documented states with 2026 income caps, responsible Medicaid agency, official .gov template URL, product model, status, and price. Prefer this for facts.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://millertrustguide.com/.well-known/openapi.json): Read-only API describing /data/states.json and the page surface.
